QUESTION OF THE WEEK - With the Australian dollar reaching a two year low just under US$0.73 last Thursday night, economists were asked where they saw the unit at the end of 1997.

Generally, a slight improvement is expected from the current level as by the end of the year, economists said, it would be more apparent that the easing cycle had come to an end. With the spectre of interest rates removed, the strong growth, low inflation economy would help the dollar.

Going into the end of 1997, commodities were expected to be improving, and solid fundamentals underpinning the dollar -- including the ongoing process of fiscal consolidation and the improved ratings outlook -- were expected to see the unit rally.
However, there were a number who saw little improvement in the dollar over the remainder of the year.

The speculation of a rate cut, and the possibility that it would be delivered before the end of the year, were seen as contributing to the lack of a rally, as were expected surprises on the downside for both domestic and international growth.
